Text Field49.value: All analysts involved in the prepping, processing, changeover and reading of the sample – Andrew Carrillo, Guanchen Li and Muralidhar Bythatagari– were interviewed and their answers are recorded throughout this document. The sample was stored upon arrival according to the Client’s instructions. Analysts Andrew Carrillo and Guanchen Li confirmed the integrity of the sample vials throughout both the preparation and processing stages. No leaks or turbidity were observed at any point, verifying the integrity of the sample. All reagents and supplies mentioned in the material section above were stored according to the suppliers’ recommendations, and their integrity was visually verified before utilization. Moreover, each reagent and supply had valid expiration dates. During the preparation phase, Andrew Carrillo disinfected the samples using acidified bleach and placed them into a pre-disinfected storage bin. On 10 Sep 2026, prior to sample processing, Guanchen Li performed a second disinfection with acidified bleach, allowing a minimum contact time of 10 minutes before transferring the samples into the ISO 8 cleanroom (117). A final disinfection step was completed immediately before the samples were introduced into the ISO 5 Biological Safety Cabinet (BSC), E001310, located within the innermost ISO 7 cleanroom (117B). All activities were performed in accordance with MICRO-SOP-12, Rapid Scan RDI® Test using FIFU Method. The cleanroom suite used for testing (CR117, E001739) consists of three interconnected sections: the innermost ISO 7 cleanroom (117B), which opens into the middle ISO 7 buffer room (117A), and then into the outermost ISO 8 anteroom (117). A positive air pressure system is maintained throughout the suite to ensure controlled, unidirectional airflow from 117B through 117A and into 117. The ISO 5 BSC E001310, located in the innermost ISO 7 room (117B) was used for the pre-labelling and filtration steps while BSC E001309, located in the middle ISO 7 room (117A) was used for changeover steps. They were thoroughly cleaned and disinfected prior to their respective procedures in accordance with MICRO-SOP-9, Cleaning and Disinfecting Procedure for Microbiology.  Furthermore, the biosafety cabinets (BSCs) utilized during the pre-filtration process (E001310) and the changeover procedure (E001309) were current in certification and had been approved for use by both the Engineering and Quality Assurance teams

Text Field50.value: Pre-labeling and filtration activities were performed by Guanchen Li on 10 Sep 2026 within the ISO 5 biosafety cabinet (BSC E001310) located in the innermost ISO 7 cleanroom (117B). The changeover procedure was subsequently performed by the same analyst on the same date within the ISO 5 biosafety cabinet (BSC E001309) located in the middle ISO 7 cleanroom (117A). The analyst, Muralidhar Bythatagari, confirmed that the equipment E002017 was set up as per ENG-SOP-4 (Scan RDI® System – Operations (Standard C3 Quality Check and Microscope Setup and Maintenance), and the negative control and the positive control for the analyst, Guanchen Li, yielded expected results. On 10Sep2026, a rapid sterility test was performed on the sample using the ScanRDI method. The sample was initially prepared by analyst – Andrew Carrillo, processed by Guanchen Li and subsequently read by Muralidhar Bythatagari. The test revealed 1 event exhibiting circular-shaped viable microorganism that appeared in cluster, see Table 1.  Table 2 (see attached tables) presents the environmental monitoring results for ETX-260908-0694. The environmental monitoring (EM) plates were incubated for no less than 48 hours at 30–35°C and for no less than an additional five days at 20–25°C, as per MICRO-SOP-2 (Environmental Monitoring of the Cleanroom Facility). Upon review of the environmental monitoring data associated with the sterility test, no microbial growth was observed on the left and right personnel touch plates for the processor and changeover analyst, Guanchen Li. Additionally, no microbial growth was recovered from the surface contact plates or settling plates collected from BSCs E001310 and E001309. Weekly surface monitoring of the anteroom and buffer room also demonstrated no microbial recovery. However, 1 CFU (ETX-260916-0726) was recovered during weekly active air monitoring of ISO 8 Cleanroom 117 conducted on 09 Sep 2026. Differential staining morphologically identified the isolate as Gram-positive rods. It is important to note that the colony morphology of the microorganism recovered from the ISO 8 cleanroom environment differed from that of the microorganism isolated from the test sample, indicating that the environmental monitoring recovery and the sample contamination were likely unrelated events.

Text Field51.value: Furthermore, all aseptic sample manipulations were performed within ISO 5 BSCs located in ISO 7 cleanrooms (117A and 117B), where no microbial growth was detected. These ISO 5 critical processing zones operate within areas maintained at a higher positive pressure relative to the surrounding ISO 8 environment, resulting in airflow from the critical processing area toward the adjacent spaces. This airflow pattern minimizes the potential for airborne contaminants from the ISO 8 environment to enter the ISO 5 work zone. Therefore, it is unlikely that the microorganism recovered from the ISO 8 environment contributed to the contamination observed in the test sample. Furthermore, the absence of microbial recovery from analyst glove plates and ISO 5 work surface monitoring indicates that no viable contamination transfer pathway existed from the room environment, including the air, into the ISO 5 BSCs. Based on the lack of detectable environmental contamination and the controlled processing conditions, the cleanroom environment is not considered a likely source of contamination for the test sample. Monthly cleaning and disinfection of the ISO 7 cleanrooms and the associated ISO 5 Biological Safety Cabinets (BSCs) were performed using hydrogen peroxide (H₂O₂) on 16 Aug 2026 in accordance with MICRO-SOP-9, Cleaning and Disinfecting Procedure for Microbiology. During both disinfection cycles, all H₂O₂ indicators met acceptance criteria and were documented as passing. These results confirm the effectiveness of the monthly cleaning and disinfection program for all areas of Cleanroom 117, including the associated BSCs. Analyzing a 6-month sample history for GoGoMeds Select (E10747), this specific analyte " Semaglutide R 2.5mg/ml Benzyl Alcohol 0.9%" has had no prior failures using the Scan RDI method during this period. To evaluate the potential for sample-to-sample contamination, all samples processed on the same day were reviewed. All other samples processed by the same analyst and by other analysts on that day yielded negative results, indicating that cross-contamination is unlikely. Review of sample lot history indicates that there have been no other submissions of specific sample lot- 19622 from the same client for ScanRDI or any other sterility tests. Based on the observations outlined above, the possibility of contamination originating from reagents, supplies, cleanroom environment, analyst, or processing is minimal. Consequently, the likelihood of laboratory error contributing to this failure is considered minimal. Therefore, the original test result is deemed valid.
